title: As for me
goal: Mark a topic with ise, -(y)sA or -(y)A gelince, and add emphasis with ta, hem de, dA mI and işte.

intro.text: Topics come first. To set one against another, use *ise* or `-(y)sA`: *Ben çay içtim, Ayşe ise kahve*. To turn to a new one, *-(y)A gelince*: *Bana gelince…* Small words add weight: *ta İstanbul'dan* (all the way from Istanbul), *hem de nasıl* (and how), *Sen de mi?* (you too?).

vocab.en: as for me (also sana gelince, ona gelince)
as far as … goes (after the ablative: paradan yana)
all the way, as far back as (ta Kars'tan: all the way from Kars)
the very one, the very thing

exercises.text: Herkes erken gitti; Mehmet'___ sabaha kadar kaldı.
exercises.en: Everyone left early; Mehmet, though, stayed until morning.

accept: se

reject.why: *De* would mean **Mehmet too**, and it is written apart. To set Mehmet against the others, use `-(y)sA`: *Mehmet'se*.
Written apart, *ise* needs no apostrophe: *Mehmet ise*. Attached after the apostrophe, it is *Mehmet'se*.

exercises.explain: `-(y)sA` after a topic sets it against the others: *Mehmet'se*, as for Mehmet. After a name, the suffix follows an apostrophe.

exercises.question: Which sentence is correct?
options: Ben çay içtim, Ayşe ise kahve.
Ben çay içtim, ise Ayşe kahve.
Ben çay içtim, Ayşe kahve ise.
İse ben çay içtim, Ayşe kahve.

why.1: *İse* never opens the clause; it follows the topic it contrasts.
why.2: Here *ise* follows *kahve*, which reads as **if it's coffee**.
why.3: *İse* can't start a sentence, and the contrasted topic is Ayşe.

exercises.explain: *İse* follows the topic it sets against another: *Ayşe ise kahve* (and Ayşe, coffee). The verb can be left out when it's the same.

exercises.prompt: As for me, I'm staying at home.
accept: Bana gelince, ben evde kalıyorum.
Bana gelince, evde [kalıyorum|kalacağım|kalırım].
Bana gelince, ben evde kalacağım.
Bana gelince, ben evde kalırım.
[Bense|Ben ise] evde [kalıyorum|kalacağım|kalırım].
Ben evde [kalıyorum|kalacağım|kalırım].
exercises.explain: *Bana gelince* (as for me) turns the conversation to a new topic. *Bense* or *ben ise* does the same by contrast with the others.

exercises.en: They came all the way from Kars for the wedding.
exercises.explain: *Ta* stretches a distance or a time: *ta Kars'tan*, all the way from Kars. It is written as a separate word.

exercises.question: Your mother says this as you come in. What does she mean?
options: You're not late today, are you?

why.1: A plain question would be *Bugün geç mi kaldın?*, without *de*.
why.2: That would be *Bugün geç kalmadın, değil mi?*
why.3: That would be the future: *Bugün geç kalacak mısın?*

exercises.explain: *dA mI* asks with surprise or reproach whether something happens **too, again**: *Bugün de mi?*, today as well?

exercises.prompt: Bu şarkı, çocukken dinlediğim türkünün ta kendisi!
accept: This song is the very folk song I listened to as a child!
This song is the very folk song I listened to when I was a child!
This song is the very folk song I listened to when I was little!
This song is the very folk song I used to listen to [as a child|when I was a child|when I was little]!
This song is the very folk song that I [listened to|used to listen to] [as a child|when I was a child|when I was little]!
This song is the very song (that) I [listened to|used to listen to] [as a child|when I was a child|when I was little]!
This song is the very türkü (that) I [listened to|used to listen to] [as a child|when I was a child|when I was little]!
This tune is the very [folk song|song|türkü] (that) I [listened to|used to listen to] [as a child|when I was a child|when I was little]!
This is the very [folk song|song|türkü] (that) I [listened to|used to listen to] [as a child|when I was a child|when I was little]!
This [song|tune] is exactly the [folk song|song|türkü] (that) I [listened to|used to listen to] [as a child|when I was a child|when I was little]!
This [song|tune] is the same [folk song|song|türkü] (that) I [listened to|used to listen to] [as a child|when I was a child|when I was little]!
exercises.explain: *Ta kendisi* (its very self) is **the very one**: *türkünün ta kendisi*, the very folk song. The clause *çocukken dinlediğim* (that I listened to as a child) comes before its noun.

exercises.prompt: We won, and five-nil at that!
accept: Kazandık, hem de beş sıfır!
maçı kazandık, hem de beş sıfır!
Biz [kazandık|maçı kazandık], hem de beş sıfır!
exercises.explain: *Hem de* adds a stronger point after a statement: we won, and what's more, five-nil.

exercises.en: That's exactly why I didn't tell anyone.

accept: İşte

reject.why: *Ta* stretches a distance or a time. To point at the very reason, use *işte*.

exercises.hint: A small word that points: here it is, that's it.
exercises.explain: *İşte* in front of *bu yüzden* points at the reason as the very one: **that's exactly why**.

exercises.prompt: Money's not a problem for us; time is.
accept: Paradan yana sorunumuz yok, zamandan yana var.
Paradan yana sorunumuz yok, vakitten yana var.
Paradan yana sıkıntımız yok, [zamandan|vakitten] yana var.
Paradan yana bir [sorunumuz|sıkıntımız] yok, [zamandan|vakitten] yana var.
Paradan yana (bir) [sorunumuz|sıkıntımız] yok [ama|fakat] [zamandan|vakitten] yana var.
Para (bizim için) sorun değil, [zaman|vakit] (sorun).
Bizim için para sorun değil, [zaman|vakit] (sorun).
exercises.explain: *-DAn yana* (as far as … goes) frames a topic: *paradan yana*, money-wise. *Var* at the end of the second clause stands for *sorunumuz var*.

exercises.task: A friend says folk music is old-fashioned. Answer in three or four sentences. Set two topics against each other with *ise* or `-(y)sA`, and use *ta* and *hem de* once each.
models: Bence halk müziği hiç eskimedi. Gençlerin bir kısmı pop dinliyor, benim kuşağımsa türkülerle büyüdü. Bu türküler ta yüzyıllar öncesinden geliyor, hem de hâlâ her düğünde söyleniyor! Sana gelince, bir kez canlı dinlesen fikrin değişir.

Haklı olabilirsin, ama bana gelince, türküsüz bir hafta düşünemiyorum. Dedem ta çocukluğundan beri saz çalıyor; ben ise ancak geçen yıl başladım. Geçen ay bir konsere gittik, hem de açık havada: binlerce genç türkü söylüyordu!
checklist: *ise* or `-(y)sA` right after the contrasted topic: *ben ise*, *benim kuşağımsa*
*ta* with a distance or a time: *ta çocukluğundan beri*
*hem de* after a statement, adding a stronger point
The verb last, unless you invert on purpose
